How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ana, en passant

Fernanda Salgado’s gorgeous animation is a travelogue of memories, ancestral connections and the future experiences that shape one’s identity.

Rogue Trooper

Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission.

Look Back

Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists.

article_text:
David Ellison’s freshly formed Skydance Corp. is off to a rocky start on Wall Street.

He won Warner Bros. Discovery after a yearlong battle . But investors, at this point, appear to believe he wildly overpaid for the deal — that the newly merged company, dubbed Skydance Corp. , is worth nowhere near the $78 billion in cash Paramount shelled out for WBD.

As of Oct. 5, the last day of trading for WBD and Paramount Skydance (PSKY) on Nasdaq, Warner Bros. Discovery had a market capitalization of $77.7 billion and Paramount was around $11 billion. Today, Skydance has a market cap of under $40 billion — less than half the predecessor companies’ combined value.

Related Stories

'I Swear' Star Robert Aramayo on the BAFTA N-Word Incident That Overshadowed the Movie and the ‘X-Men’ Wolverine Pitch He Keeps Hearing

Lucy Liu’s 'The Pirate Queen' Expands With Graphic Novel, New Game and International Tour as Creator Eloise Singer Joins BAFTA Breakthrough Cohort (EXCLUSIVE)

On Wednesday, Skydance’s stock plunged 22% . That came after the company distributed about 471 million warrants giving holders of Paramount Skydance’s PSKY Class B shares the option to purchase stock in the new company for $12/share.

What happened? On Tuesday after the market close, the New York Stock Exchange made a technical adjustment to Skydance’s share price, reducing it by 19.4 cents, to account for the issuance of the warrants (trading on NYSE as “SKYD.WS”). The speculation is that index funds sold off the warrants they held when those start trading; that, in turn, was interpreted as a sell-off event by automated trading systems, which pushed down the price of SKYD stock. Skydance issued a press release Wednesday after market close noting that the warrants represent only around 9% of its Class B common stock.

According to Skydance, the implied value with the warrant distribution would have given Skydance a market cap of $45.6 billion at the $9.07/share price of the Class B stock — and that the value of the warrants at $2.20 each was around $1 billion (for total equity value of $46.6 billion for the company). With the stock drop Wednesday, the market cap skidded to around $36 billion. On Thursday, Skydance stock rebounded slightly, closing up 2.8% to $7.26, bringing the company’s market cap to $36.6 billion (not including the value of warrants, which had a closing price Thursday of $2.96 each).

But beyond the disruption from the issuance of the stock warrants, there’s skepticism among analysts and credit-rating agencies that Skydance can hit the numbers the company’s top brass have projected. Ellison and his team will have to prove to Wall Street they can achieve the $6 billion cost savings (on an annualized basis over the next three years) in the new company while continuing to invest in content — including more than 30 films released theatrically per year — as well as the rest of the business. All the while, Skydance will have to pay down its massive debt load. As it currently stands, the company’s interest payments alone will be north of $6 billion per year.

With the merger’s closing, Paramount paid WBD shareholders an amount in cash equal to $31.01666668 per share for a total of about $78 billion. Under the terms of the deal, Paramount also is assuming WBD’s debt ($33.1 billion as of the end of June), leaving the merged company’s net debt at nearly $80 billion .

Meanwhile, Skydance’s Class B investors don’t have a say in corporate governance issues. The Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners are the sole holders of Skydance’s Class A stock, giving them 100% control the voting shares. (Those Class A shares do not have intrinsic value but have the option for each share to be converted into 1.5 Class B shares, according to a Skydance SEC filing .)

So far, the biggest winners from the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger have been WBD shareholders — including former Warner Bros. Discovery chief David Zaslav , who cashed out his stock and options in the company for a total of $606.1 million (before taxes).

That said, some market watchers see Skydance as an attractive investment after Wednesday’s stock drop.

“There could be a buying opportunity in Skydance stock because the company’s share count hasn’t changed much with the warrant issuance” and “Skydance’s outlook hasn’t changed,” Barron’s associate editor Andrew Bary wrote in an Oct. 14 article . While the warrants, with the $12/share price, are currently underwater, they have value based on option pricing models “due to the long maturity of 10 years and the possibility that Skydance stock will rally in the coming years,” Bary added.

article_text:
Welcome to The Weekend Read — Deadline’s collection of long-form features, curated here just in case you missed them during the week.

And what a week it’s been! With the true blue results from the mid-terms, what might this mean for the industry? Read our analysis and coverage from election night.

We’ve also got our review of Godzilla Minus Zero , a sit-down with Primetime ‘s Skyler Gisondo, a chat with Trudie Styler about her two new projects and a close-up on the innovations happening over at Korean banner Studio N. Check out all these and more linked below.

Can The Blue Tsunami Save Hollywood? Image Credit: Getty Images American voters issued a stunning rebuke of the Trump Administration on Tuesday night by electing Democrats to take control of both chambers of Congress come January. Among the many implications for Hollywood in the 2026 midterm election results, the efforts to enact a federal tax incentive for U.S. film and television production might have just hit an unexpected roadblock. Lawmakers introduced the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in September to create a first-of-its-kind tax credit designed to lure production back to the United States. The hope has been that the legislation could be attached to an end-of-year budget bill facing a vote by December 11 and land on the President’s desk soon after. Read the analysis here Read ‘A Night of Many Firsts in Mid-Term Elections’ here Read ‘What Stood Out In Media Mid-Terms Coverage’ here

The ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review Image Credit: Toho With 2023’s monster hit Godzilla Minus One, Takashi Yamazaki became only the second director after Stanley Kubrick and 2001: A Space Odyssey to take home the Visual Effects Academy Award, and his film became the only Godzilla movie in 70 years to win an Oscar. Naturally, that all calls for a sequel, doesn’t it? The filmmaker wasn’t sure since he didn’t want to disappoint the legions of fans of the first film, a Japanese Kaiju cinema masterpiece which, unlike most of the Godzilla films, really succeeded in part because of the emotional human story it also had to tell. Well, it is nice to say he hasn’t forgotten that aspect, even as Godzilla Minus Zero , set two years after the first, has gone much bigger and was “filmed for IMAX”. The fabulous Scope visual palette is still there but adding the IMAX brand turns out to complement it rather than smother it. Read the full review here

Skyler Gisondo Talks ‘Primetime’ Image Credit: A24 You’d think in the last year, especially given that he’s coming off a successful outing as Jimmy Olsen in James Gunn’s Superman , that Skyler Gisondo would imagine himself as pretty cool. Though, jokingly, by his own account, nothing quite topped appearing in Phoebe Bridgers ’ “Lost Boys” music video. “I never felt cooler in my life than being in a Phoebe Bridgers music video,” he tells Deadline, recalling how the appearance prompted texts from people he hadn’t heard from in 15 years, saying, “Dude, I had no idea you were so cool.” On the day of our conversation, Gisondo is in Florida, perched at a nearby playground beneath a vibrant blue sky. Bright-eyed, handsomely freckle-faced and dressed in colorful attire, he is all smiles and eager to chat. Ironically, it’s a decidedly sunny setting for a conversation about Primetime , Lance Oppenheim ’s dark, satirical thriller. Read the interview here

Trudie Styler Has Been (Very) Busy Making Films Image Credit: Josh Telles/ Deadline Trudie Styler arrives at the London offices of Maven Screen Media , her joint production company with Celine Rattray , bearing gifts: bottles of organic extra virgin olive oil. Featuring Styler and husband Sting ’s names on the label, they are the last of a batch made from the 2025 olive harvest at Villa Il Palagio, their beloved 16th Century estate in Tuscany. She is not here to talk about her long love affair with Italy, however, but rather back-to-back directorial feature film credits Up Against It and The Reception as well as her and Rattray’s commitment to championing female-driven storytelling. Read the interview here

Why Studio N CEO Mikyung Kwon Is Game To Take Creative Gambles Image Credit: Hulu/Courtesy Mikyung (Michelle) Kwon is not afraid to take a risk. As CEO of Studio N, the Korean production arm of Webtoon Entertainment, she’s helped to build a prolific slate of webcomic screen adaptations including Netflix hits Bloodhounds and The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call as well as last year’s Korean box office hit My Daughter is a Zombie. But now the former CJ ENM and Disney Korea exec is taking what she says is the biggest creative gamble of her career to date with Disney+ romantacy series The Remarried Empress . The hugely anticipated show dropped its first four episodes on November 3 on Disney+ and Hulu, one day earlier than the originally scheduled November 4 premiere date thanks to early buzz from fans. The show’s trailer surpassed a whopping 13 million views in the first 48 hours on YouTube when it launched in September. “This project will define my life,” Kwon tells Deadline of Studio N’s most ambitious and expensive production to date. “I have a lot of anxiety and expectation at the same time right now.” Read the interview here

‘Toy Story 5’s Andrew Stanton Talks Taylor Swift, Kids’ Tech Issues & More Image Credit: Disney For the better part of three decades, Woody ( Tom Hanks ), Buzz ( Tim Allen ), and the gang have kept audiences company through the ups and downs of growing up. Now, Toy Story 5 finds the franchise entering a new chapter, with Jessie ( Joan Cusack ) taking center stage and technology changing the way children play. Writer-director Andrew Stanton helps usher in a new group of characters: Lilypad (Greta Lee), a frog-framed tablet, and Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), a confident young girl who marches to the beat of her own drum. Alongside the familiar faces, the new toys bring fresh possibilities to a story that still has plenty to say about childhood and the evolution of social connection. Below, Stanton talks to Deadline about developing another entry, digging deeper into Jessie’s backstory, and the cherry on top of the cake: Taylor Swift’s new pop-country single, “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Read the interview here

article_text:
The actor Selma Blair was arrested on Sunday at John F Kennedy airport in New York after she allegedly attacked two flight attendants on a Delta Air Lines flight, and separately charged with two counts of assault for allegedly kicking a police officer and a nurse after landing.

Blair’s arrest happened at about 11pm, after Port Authority of New York and New Jersey officials said they responded to a call “about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Air Lines flight 938 which was parked at the gate” at JFK after arriving from Los Angeles.

The 54-year-old “was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation”, the port authority said on Monday. “Two flight attendants also reported injuries, and one was transported to the hospital for further evaluation.”

Several news outlets on Monday reported that Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open the airplane door.

The Guardian has reached out to Blair’s representatives for additional comment. Her publicist told the Hollywood Reporter: “Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is [now] in stable condition.”

The FBI, which handles reports of crimes on airplanes, has issued Blair a notice charging her with assault related to her actions aboard the aircraft, according to a federal law enforcement official who spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak publicly about the matter.

Those charges will be handled through the petty violations court in federal court in Brooklyn. No date has been set for Blair’s appearance.

Separately, Blair was charged on Monday night at a court in Queens with two counts of second-degree assault, for allegedly assaulting a police officer who was taking her to hospital after the flight, as well as a nurse after she arrived there.

In charging documents, a police officer taking her to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center alleged that while she was securing Blair to a stretcher, Blair pulled a leg from the straps and kicked her repeatedly around the face, neck and chest, causing serious pain and substantial swelling. A nurse who was moving Blair in hospital alleged the actor then kicked her in the chest, causing substantial pain.

On Monday night, a judge set Blair’s bail at $20,000 cash or $60,000 bond and set the next hearing for January. Blair then left court with her lawyers.

Details of what happened aboard the aircraft weren’t immediately disclosed by the airline, police or the FBI, which was investigating, but a Delta spokesperson said the airline “has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first”.

An air traffic control audio recording from the flight Blair was on captured the pilot saying “one flight attendant and one passenger … sustained some minor injuries – a bloody nose as well as some bite marks”.

“I don’t think we need an ambulance or anything like that – but we just want to get some medical personnel at the gate to look at their injuries,” the pilot said, according to the recording, a copy of which was published by NBC Los Angeles.

The flight controller replied that paramedics were approaching the gate – and that law enforcement was already there.

Sunday marked at least the second time Blair was reported to be involved in an incident on a plane. In 2016, she reportedly began screaming uncontrollably before being removed on a stretcher while on a Los Angeles-bound flight from Cancún, Mexico.

Blair apologized after the earlier episode, saying that she “mixed alcohol with medication”.

“That caused me to black out and led me to say and do things that I deeply regret,” Blair said at the time.

The actor has also made news headlines for a 2018 multiple sclerosis diagnosis . And in February 2024, she apologized for an Islamophobic comment on social media.

Blair’s starring film credits include Cruel Intentions, Legally Blonde and Hellboy. She earned a best spoken word album for children nomination at the 2011 Grammy awards for her work on Anne Frank: The Diary of a Young Girl – The Definitive Edition.

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "It’s not even Halloween but already time to set your 2027 viewing calendar. Coming to Criterion on Blu-ray are Claire Denis’ feature debut, Chocolat , a film whose colors and textures demand a higher, and Mike Leigh’s Career Girls , which will resonate differently after the vision of female friendship in his great, potentially final film Tender Loving Care . article_text:
It’s not even Halloween but already time to set your 2027 viewing calendar. Coming to Criterion on Blu-ray are Claire Denis’ feature debut, Chocolat , a film whose colors and textures demand a higher, and Mike Leigh’s Career Girls , which will resonate differently after the vision of female friendship in his great, potentially final film Tender Loving Care . New and on 4K is John Boorman’s Deliverance , with “Dueling Banjos” screeching in restored sound; upgrade-wise, Bong Joon-ho’s Parasite is jumping to 4K from its 2021 disc, while Midnight Cowboy is brought to full resolution for the first time since its 2018 debut.

The most essential release to start 2027, though, is a Blu-ray set of Martin Scorsese’s World Cinema Project. The sixth edition of arguably Criterion’s finest ongoing project features Flora Gomes’ Morta Nega (from Guinea-Bissau), Luis Sérgio Person’s São Paulo, Incorporated (from Brazil), Timité Bassori’s The Woman with the Knife (from Côte d’Ivoire), and Bahram Beyzai’s The Stranger and the Fog (from Iran). Once on the edge of extinction, these films are given the ideal, as Richard Linklater would say , forever home.

article_text:
W.M.ヴォーリズ設計【神戸女学院】は、創立150年余り関西が誇る名門です。壮麗にして優雅な姿は、学校建築の最高傑作と呼ばれています。約4万坪の敷地には12棟もの重要文化財の建物が…。普段一般の人が立ち入ることができないサンクチュアリ＝聖域に内田有紀さんが迫ります。

title_original: 《有用的人》：活著沒有完美落地的時候
title_zh: 《有用的人》：活著沒有完美落地的時候
summary_zh: 来源摘录：李芸嬋無疑傾注了專心育兒多年後，對中產階級家庭看似安定、實則脆弱的敏銳體察，而小品日常的微觀溫柔，在電影的巨幅之下則需要更穩健的鏡頭、更厚實的戲劇結構，《有用的人》的呈現其實體現出了不同階級、不同關係位置之間，依然有著一條幽深峽谷似的代溝。然而，電影仍坦白承認了，面對浩瀚命運時，人的無能為力與逃避。 這篇文章 《有用的人》：活著沒有完美落地的時候 最早出現於 釀電影 。
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "quote", "text": "撰文／雀雀 劇照提供／台北金馬影展執行委員會 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "歷來作品總有高度奇幻元素的李芸嬋，在 22 年後憑《有用的人》（To be Ordinary，2026）獲第 33 屆釜山國際影展「最佳導演」獎，該作亦為李芸嬋戮力接軌，欲進入臺灣新電影的誠意嘗試。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作為在國片復甦前期便崛起的新銳女導演，李芸嬋出道時乘著強烈的繪本式魔幻風格羽翼，讓女性角色的身體、容貌焦慮，在她堆疊的當代消費文化與戀物符號裡自信舒展。至少，2004 年到 2010 年的李芸嬋是這樣子的。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那麼從《人魚朵朵》（The Shoe Fairy，2006）到《有用的人》，李芸嬋發生了什麼事？沒事，她只是結了婚、生小孩了而已。釜山國際影展連續兩年把「最佳導演」獎頒給臺灣女導演，上一屆是舒淇執導的《女孩》（Girl，2025），顯然韓國人真的很想知道：在臺灣女導演的眼中，她們想拍的家庭電影，究竟是什麼模樣？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "似乎是在 《囍宴》（The Wedding Banquet，1993） 、 《一一》（Yi Yi：A One and a Two，2000） 、 《陽光普照》（A Sun，2019） 等片之後，以《女孩》與《有用的人》的女導演視角，有意識地補上了臺灣新電影的兩性平衡敘事。臺灣女導演近年拍出不少優秀的家庭電影，如《幸福路上》（On Happiness Road，2017）、 《美國女孩》（American Girl，2021） 和《哈勇家》（GAGA，2022）等作，甚至是由男性導演執導的 《孤味》（Little Big Women，2020） 、 《小曉》（Trouble Girl，2023） 等作，也都溫柔以女性視角觀照當代女性集體面貌。", "links": [{"text": "《囍宴》（The Wedding "paragraph", "text": "令人玩味的是，導演在開篇刻意遮蔽了哥哥昱杰（謝展榮飾）的臉龐，此番調度冷靜預示著這號人物的謎樣存在，卻也更惹人好奇：這個人後來怎麼了？他在整部電影裡，究竟是在什麼樣的位置上？ 被撞得下半身不遂的他，成為這個家庭的沉重象徵，家庭成員也不得不面對感情裂痕、經濟停滯等僵局。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "若說《女孩》是舒淇挖掘成長記憶中，對家庭之愛與恐懼的複合夢境，那麼《有用的人》便是李芸嬋眼中的，關於臺灣、臺北的中產家庭生存焦慮。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1983 年，臺灣新電影《兒子的大玩偶》（The Sandwich Man，1983）第三部〈蘋果的滋味〉（The Sandwich Man），貧困工人遭美軍車輛撞斷腿，全家人卻因禍得福、嚐到象徵美援與富裕的紅蘋果，卓勝利演出了被撞斷腿的江阿發、笑得真誠的草根味。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "而半個世紀過去，《有用的人》的兒子被富裕老先生撞了，肇事者為了贖罪，竟將市價不斐的房產廉價折抵為賠償金，讓這一工薪家庭就此搬進了望塵莫及的高級新居。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/VYvhGy7CFLPTOy4fqP0CggL8cB9-Vsi5UN459YjP7Fk/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/a0a5efa8-7267-4a39-8621-64a551e05dc0.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", 臺灣經濟歷經數十年發展，以前的窮人只住得起違建，現在是連市郊的老公寓也租不起。然而，這個家庭卻用兒子的雙腿，換來了安身立命的明亮客廳。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當一家人圍坐在餐廳吃晚餐，炒菜上桌、擺上碗筷雖都是日常，空氣中卻瀰漫著用哥哥的殘缺折現而來的幸福，一家四口的心底，總有揮之不去的代償感，畢竟收下新房子的道德困境，早已被動地向命運妥協。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》用肉身獻祭，換取了一份不可思議的好事，是你的話，會要嗎？一如多年來，臺灣經濟看似起飛了，物質空間也變大了，但現代臺灣人的幸福指數，真的變高了嗎？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "臺灣女性導演在家庭題材上的深耕，近年是有目共睹，阮鳳儀在《美國女孩》對母女相愛相殺的纖毫畢現，陳潔瑤在《哈勇家》則是對臺灣原住民傳統文化的 GAGA 精神與現代世俗衝擊有著宏觀凝視。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸嬋無疑傾注了專心育兒多年後，對中產階級家庭看似安定、實則脆弱的敏銳體察，而小品日常的微觀溫柔，在電影的巨幅之下則需要更穩健的鏡頭、更厚實的戲劇結構，《有用的人》的呈現其實體現出了不同階級、不同關係位置之間，依然有著一條幽深峽谷似的代溝。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/n-lXqr16MRjwLLkSiHp70cJavA3PiJmv-ye784B4L2M/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/da374ec5-1a7c-4bcd-9db8-00cb6dc5aabb.jpg", "alt": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影前半段氛圍極佳，鏡頭的流動也牽引出觀眾想繼續看下去的慾望，畫面低調而克制地呈現出艱辛的復健過程、辛勞而佝僂的家人背影，其中皆有日常邊緣的詩意質地；然而，隨著後段劇情發展的出乎意料，敘事節奏與剪接也開始令人愈發困惑（也像是戲裡戲外的人，或許都難以接受此般生命走向所致）。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "張詩盈飾演的母親，則是一個被生活、生命逼到極限，會在陽臺突然砸爛鳥巢的平凡人。從一開始，母親對兒子告白「我在二十年前，就下定決心要把你養大」的強大意念，到後來瀕臨精神崩潰的空洞眼神，都將照護者的崩潰、母愛的執念與自我的消磨，一路詮釋得令人不忍卒睹。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": 撰文／雀雀 劇照提供／台北金馬影展執行委員會 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

歷來作品總有高度奇幻元素的李芸嬋，在 22 年後憑《有用的人》（To be Ordinary，2026）獲第 33 屆釜山國際影展「最佳導演」獎，該作亦為李芸嬋戮力接軌，欲進入臺灣新電影的誠意嘗試。

作為在國片復甦前期便崛起的新銳女導演，李芸嬋出道時乘著強烈的繪本式魔幻風格羽翼，讓女性角色的身體、容貌焦慮，在她堆疊的當代消費文化與戀物符號裡自信舒展。至少，2004 年到 2010 年的李芸嬋是這樣子的。

那麼從《人魚朵朵》（The Shoe Fairy，2006）到《有用的人》，李芸嬋發生了什麼事？沒事，她只是結了婚、生小孩了而已。釜山國際影展連續兩年把「最佳導演」獎頒給臺灣女導演，上一屆是舒淇執導的《女孩》（Girl，2025），顯然韓國人真的很想知道：在臺灣女導演的眼中，她們想拍的家庭電影，究竟是什麼模樣？

似乎是在 《囍宴》（The Wedding Banquet，1993） 、 《一一》（Yi Yi：A One and a Two，2000） 、 《陽光普照》（A Sun，2019） 等片之後，以《女孩》與《有用的人》的女導演視角，有意識地補上了臺灣新電影的兩性平衡敘事。臺灣女導演近年拍出不少優秀的家庭電影，如《幸福路上》（On Happiness Road，2017）、 《美國女孩》（American Girl，2021） 和《哈勇家》（GAGA，2022）等作，甚至是由男性導演執導的 《孤味》（Little Big Women，2020） 、 《小曉》（Trouble Girl，2023） 等作，也都溫柔以女性視角觀照當代女性集體面貌。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

《有用的人》看似承接了這條譜系，卻微妙地將攝影機架設在一個更為尷尬、也更具生存危機感中產夾縫裡。 開場宛如致敬 《南國再見，南國》（Goodbye South, Goodbye，1996） 般，帶著預警意味的馳騁鏡頭以車禍戛然銜接一顆長鏡頭，直接撞碎了家庭的平靜日常。

令人玩味的是，導演在開篇刻意遮蔽了哥哥昱杰（謝展榮飾）的臉龐，此番調度冷靜預示著這號人物的謎樣存在，卻也更惹人好奇：這個人後來怎麼了？他在整部電影裡，究竟是在什麼樣的位置上？ 被撞得下半身不遂的他，成為這個家庭的沉重象徵，家庭成員也不得不面對感情裂痕、經濟停滯等僵局。

若說《女孩》是舒淇挖掘成長記憶中，對家庭之愛與恐懼的複合夢境，那麼《有用的人》便是李芸嬋眼中的，關於臺灣、臺北的中產家庭生存焦慮。

1983 年，臺灣新電影《兒子的大玩偶》（The Sandwich Man，1983）第三部〈蘋果的滋味〉（The Sandwich Man），貧困工人遭美軍車輛撞斷腿，全家人卻因禍得福、嚐到象徵美援與富裕的紅蘋果，卓勝利演出了被撞斷腿的江阿發、笑得真誠的草根味。

而半個世紀過去，《有用的人》的兒子被富裕老先生撞了，肇事者為了贖罪，竟將市價不斐的房產廉價折抵為賠償金，讓這一工薪家庭就此搬進了望塵莫及的高級新居。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

即使妹妹並不想嚐「新房子的滋味」，一家人礙於現實還是搬進去了，這份賠償是全片最荒謬、殘酷且諷刺的一環設計， 臺灣經濟歷經數十年發展，以前的窮人只住得起違建，現在是連市郊的老公寓也租不起。然而，這個家庭卻用兒子的雙腿，換來了安身立命的明亮客廳。

當一家人圍坐在餐廳吃晚餐，炒菜上桌、擺上碗筷雖都是日常，空氣中卻瀰漫著用哥哥的殘缺折現而來的幸福，一家四口的心底，總有揮之不去的代償感，畢竟收下新房子的道德困境，早已被動地向命運妥協。

《有用的人》用肉身獻祭，換取了一份不可思議的好事，是你的話，會要嗎？一如多年來，臺灣經濟看似起飛了，物質空間也變大了，但現代臺灣人的幸福指數，真的變高了嗎？

臺灣女性導演在家庭題材上的深耕，近年是有目共睹，阮鳳儀在《美國女孩》對母女相愛相殺的纖毫畢現，陳潔瑤在《哈勇家》則是對臺灣原住民傳統文化的 GAGA 精神與現代世俗衝擊有著宏觀凝視。

李芸嬋無疑傾注了專心育兒多年後，對中產階級家庭看似安定、實則脆弱的敏銳體察，而小品日常的微觀溫柔，在電影的巨幅之下則需要更穩健的鏡頭、更厚實的戲劇結構，《有用的人》的呈現其實體現出了不同階級、不同關係位置之間，依然有著一條幽深峽谷似的代溝。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

電影前半段氛圍極佳，鏡頭的流動也牽引出觀眾想繼續看下去的慾望，畫面低調而克制地呈現出艱辛的復健過程、辛勞而佝僂的家人背影，其中皆有日常邊緣的詩意質地；然而，隨著後段劇情發展的出乎意料，敘事節奏與剪接也開始令人愈發困惑（也像是戲裡戲外的人，或許都難以接受此般生命走向所致）。

張詩盈飾演的母親，則是一個被生活、生命逼到極限，會在陽臺突然砸爛鳥巢的平凡人。從一開始，母親對兒子告白「我在二十年前，就下定決心要把你養大」的強大意念，到後來瀕臨精神崩潰的空洞眼神，都將照護者的崩潰、母愛的執念與自我的消磨，一路詮釋得令人不忍卒睹。

母親在極度壓抑下的精神崩潰，理應是全片最核心，也最能照見中產家庭女性困境的處理，卻是重重舉起、輕輕放下，就像是在經歷萬般痛苦後的女人，仍要告訴自己必須撐住，甚至要盡量看起來若無其事。（或許這樣的違和感也是導演想要的？）

而這也不免讓人思索，創作者在書寫社會邊緣的敘事時，究竟能夠碰觸到何種極限？若要恪守絕不消費他人苦難的道德底線，劇情線該就此收束嗎？或者，女兒與母親的枕邊對話，可以深入、赤裸，甚至殘酷到何種地步呢？

電影裡的母女呈現，既無力接合生命共同的、隱微的創傷，也沒能狗血地大吵一架、把話說開，僅僅只是聊到最後，將關係裡無法更進一步的種子，埋在觀眾的心中。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

而在學校課堂上，老師用平靜的語調講解著「疏果」原理：為了讓留在枝頭的玉米長得飽滿、碩大，農人必須狠心摘除發育不良的果實。這段看似不經意的教學，是整部電影的重要隱喻之一，當代社會何嘗不是時時刻刻都進行著殘酷的「疏果」？

失業的中年人、身心障礙的青年、疲憊脫序的母親，在功利機器的運轉下，都將被視為消耗養分的贅瘤；甚至，在家庭內部，妹妹也因家庭資源、雙親目光皆放在身障的哥哥身上，而不得不提早學會獨自準備簡單的便食、自己買自己的衛生棉，以一種被「疏果」的孤獨姿態早熟長大。

飾演妹妹的陳品嫙，從第一顆在運動會的直視鏡頭，到守著空蕩客廳、獨自吃食的落寞神情，孤獨成長的身影特別令人心疼。在多年之後，當長大成人的妹妹來到安養院探望肇事老先生，老人家早已失智，只是木然地叮囑：「將來做一個有用的人。」

生命的韌性，就在女孩被無常狠狠掠過、一切既有秩序被連根拔起之後，她只能自己確立自己的生活，並在其中讓自己長大。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

楊一展交出一次具說服力的演出。他所飾演的父親，精準呈現出中年失業男性的自尊與挫敗，他在樓梯間與妻子企圖「把話講開」的隱忍、在廚房熟練炒菜的身影，就像所有中年父親心中有苦、卻無法示弱時，就只好轉頭默默顧家的背影。

謝展榮飾演的哥哥則是曖曖內含光，不論是在輪椅上的受挫與振作、與家人相處的溫柔與自然，毫無煽情氣息，也演出少年剛長出成年人肩膀的質地。哥哥努力考取駕照、靠線上接案自立，那份在殘缺中試圖重建生活的姿態，也早已超越了世俗對「有用」的窄化定義。

即使無常再度帶著死神的陰影降臨，那些在陣痛中勉力牽起的手，依然幾度替殘破的家庭，留下了最柔軟的微光。

釜山國際影展之目光，重視亞洲各國在時代變遷下的現實切片，今年由《有用的人》為臺灣電影代表，無疑是李芸嬋「穿透中產日常、直視脆弱無常」的創作自覺，有效地擊中了國際選片人對東亞現代家庭困境的共鳴。

《有用的人》電影劇照／劇照提供：台北金馬影展執行委員會

不過，該作卻在同年度的金馬獎入圍名單上，面臨嚴峻的審美分期，這也恰恰映射出當代亞洲影展在評審團機制下的審美分眾化；在金馬複選評審的決定下，《有用的人》最終並未入圍，這也不免讓人想起《孤味》在該屆台北電影獎入圍名單中全軍覆沒，後來卻獲得金馬獎最佳女演員獎的既視感。

可能後半段的戲劇轉折，與角色情緒偶發的斷裂感，就是評審眼中有待「疏果」的枝枒。但是，這部電影真的需要被大刀闊斧地，修剪得更具有得獎體質嗎？釜山影展評審的答案，顯然是否定的。 畢竟電影坦白承認了，面對浩瀚命運時，人的無能為力與逃避。

中文的「有用的人」，與英文店名的「To Be Ordinary」，或許就是李芸嬋結婚生子 16 年來的沉澱與結論。為人父母若只能有一個願望的話，都會希望孩子此生能當個「平常的人」。

因為真正懂得在巨大的無常面前，誠實地活過、愛過、痛過，還能倖存下來、能完美落地，已絕非易事，而這和李芸嬋生來就走在菁英道路上的生命經驗，是如此地不同。

《釀電影》，「如果月亮背面是汪洋，日光就是生命的海流──金馬 63 專題」主視覺。／圖像提供：釀電影（設計：林雅萱）

月亮是最古早的電視，而電影百年的靈光， 是被迫倒下的巨樹身後，有眾人為祂記憶。

如果月亮背面是汪洋， 日光就是生命的海流。

article_text:
政治と芸術、その複雑な関係を見つめる──「共時的星叢──時を共にした星たち 越境する芸術のまなざし」【EDITOR’S NOTES】

異なる文化や思想との出会いは、新たな芸術表現を生み出す契機となる一方、その背景には複雑な政治的・社会的関係が存在することもある。東京都現代美術館で開催中の「共時的星叢」から、日本統治期から戦後にかけての台湾で生まれた表現と、その背景にある歴史をたどる。

芸術表現は、作家個人の内発的な問いだけでなく、時代ごとの社会状況や政治体制、異なる思想や価値観との接触など、さまざまな要因の影響を受けながら育まれる。しかし、その「影響関係」が常に対等なものとは限らない。東京都現代美術館で開催中の「共時的星叢──時を共にした星たち 越境する芸術のまなざし」は、20世紀前半の台湾と日本を中心とする芸術の交流を通じて、その複雑な関係を浮かび上がらせる。

本展がたどるのは、20世紀前半の台湾と日本を中心に、東アジアの作家や詩人たちが同じ時代を生きるなかで、どのように表現をつくり上げていったのかという歴史だ。西洋で生まれた近代美術が日本へ、さらに台湾へと伝わっていったという一本の系譜として描くのではなく、それぞれの土地で生まれた表現や交流を同時代の動きとして捉え直そうとしている。その背景にあるのが、1895年から1945年まで続いた日本による台湾統治だ。会場には絵画や彫刻だけでなく、文学、映画、音楽、演劇、雑誌や書簡までが並ぶ。

日本による統治が始まる以前の台湾では、福建など中国大陸南部に由来する書画文化や、廟を彩る彫刻、儀礼に関わる工芸など、多様な造形文化が育まれていた。しかし1895年に日本の植民地統治が始まると、西洋近代美術の概念や美術教育、公募展などの制度が日本を通じて導入され、台湾の美術を取り巻く環境は変化していった。

その象徴が、1927年に始まった台湾美術展覧会（台展）だ。日本の帝国美術院展覧会（帝展）を参考に設けられたこの公募展では、台湾の風土や暮らしを題材とする「地方色」が作品評価の重要な観点の一つとなった。会場に並ぶ郭雪湖《南街殷賑》（1930）の彩色下絵は、その一例だ。大稲埕（ダーダオチェン）で生まれ育った郭が、祖先やさまよう霊を供養する伝統行事「中元普渡」でにぎわう地元の街を題材に選んだこの作品は、第4回台展で台展賞を受賞している。

ただし、何が「台湾らしい」と評価されるのか、その基準もまた、植民地統治下の美術制度と無関係ではなかった。

日中戦争が始まる1937年以降、台湾では、日本の戦時体制の強化に伴い、文化活動や芸術表現に対する統制も強まっていった。日中戦争の勃発後、台湾総督府は皇民化政策を本格化させ、日本語使用の推進や新聞の漢文欄の廃止など、生活や文化の日本化を進めた。

第5章「描いた／描かせた のは誰か」には、台湾・新竹出身の李澤藩が日の丸を手に出征兵を見送る人々を描いた《出征の見送り》（1938）と、日本の洋画家・鶴田吾郎が、日本軍の戦争遂行のために台湾先住民族の人々を動員して構成された高砂義勇隊を題材とする《義勇隊を送る高砂族》（1944）が並ぶ。美術や文学が戦時体制へと組み込まれていくなか、ここでは作家が「何を描いたか」だけでなく、「なぜそれを描くことになったのか」までが問われている。

1945年の日本の敗戦によって植民地統治は終わり、台湾では中華民国による統治が始まった。しかし、その後も芸術表現をめぐる政治的な制約は続いた。なくなったわけではない。戦後、台湾では美術や文学、演劇などの活動が再び活発になる一方、1947年の二・二八事件では、中華民国政府による武力弾圧が起き、1949年から1987年まで続いた戒厳令下では、国民党政権による政治的弾圧が広がった。芸術家や文学者も、その対象となった。最終章「長い白夜」には、1954年に処刑された劇作家・簡国賢が妻に宛てた最後の手紙など、弾圧によって創作だけでなく、日常や命までも奪われた人々の存在を伝える資料も並ぶ。また、国民党政権は自らを「中華文化の正統な継承者」と位置付け、文化政策を推進した。戒厳体制下の検閲や政治的弾圧と、こうした政策や政治的な統制は、台湾の芸術表現にも影響を及ぼした。

台展の「地方色」、戦時下の「描いた／描かせた」、戦後の「正統」をめぐる文化政策。時代や政治体制の変化とともに、芸術表現を取り巻く制度や価値観も変容していった。本展で目にしたのは、そうした時代の条件と向き合いながら、異なる文化や思想との接触を通じて、それぞれの表現を模索し続けた作家たちの姿だ。

article_text:
Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 Cannes coverage. The film opens in theaters on October 9.

A soft upright piano playing “Amazing Grace” drapes in warmly over the opening image of Fjord : a powder-blue-hued glacial mountain towering over the glistening Norwegian fjord around which Lisbet (Renate Reinsve) and Mihai Gheorghiu (Sebastian Stan) have resettled their seven-person family. Lisbet, a Norwegian nurse, and Mihai, a Romanian aeronautical engineer, just moved to the idyllic seaside village in Norway from Bucharest, where their devout evangelical Christian faith held a much better reputation in the conservative home country of writer-director Cristian Mungiu, who’s aimed his last two features ( Graduation , R.M.N. ) at the pitfalls of its uber-traditional society.

The Gheorghius don’t necessarily come across as a good hang. They spend all their free time singing worship songs and reading scripture, and insist their children do the same. The two teenage eldest of the five, chronic rule-followers Elia (Vanessa Ceban) and Emmanuel (Jonathan Ciprian Breazu), have no access to the internet, much less YouTube. When she sees an electric piano at school, Elia can’t help but play a hymn, just like her father did when he was touring the campus. Both are lightly reprimanded by the Norwegians near them. “We don’t do evangelism at school,” Mats, their neighbor, tells Elia with a smile. Even their outfits are conservative: long, unflattering grey skirts and Mennonite-esque hair tied up for Lisbet, turtlenecks and blazers for Mihai.

Their poised stance against homosexuality is abominable, their casual tendency to spank their children a reprehensible relic of generations past. Both are anachronisms in a modern global age that sees the backwards ideological strongholds as thought crimes—in Norway, actual crimes. So much so that, in the middle of the afternoon, after a teacher develops reason to believe they’ve been spanked, Child Protective Services arrive unannounced to take the children into custody while they investigate the situation. But, like anyone else, the Gheorghius deserve their liberties and a proper defense in court from the iron-fisted Norwegian powers that have gone so far left that they’ve come back around to the right—flown the country so close to the sun of liberalism that they’ve begun to burn the minorities who live there. (“They never had communism,” Mihai remarks critically.)

Several key questions run through the veins of Fjord . The first is whether or not the Gheorghius are physically abusing their children. But when they openly admit to occasionally spanking them, and the children say the same, the question transforms: should parents be allowed to do this? If not, what should be the punishment for parents? Should their children be legally seized for the remainder of their youth? Another question, one the film refuses to weigh in on for its audience, hangs in the balance: at what point does spanking become beating or physical abuse?

Civil and criminal trials hang over Lisbet and Mihai’s baffled heads like a spectre of familial death as they prepare for their internationally publicized civil trial, which CPS keeps postponing in hopes of the criminal trial taking place first—one that will almost certainly find the Gheorghius guilty per Norwegian legislation. In a culture-versus-law showdown for the ages, the Gheorghius ask Mia (Lisa Carlehed)—a liberal atheist neighbor whose wrist-cutting, fuck-saying, and rule-breaking daughter becomes an influence on Elia and Emmanuel—to represent them. Mia agrees, finding the state’s stance harsh and damaging to the children in light of something as minor as spanking when the kids want to go home, the Gheorghius have promised never to do it again, and they clearly didn’t know they were committing a crime in the first place. Together, they take a religious-persecution angle that suggests the Gheorghius are facing discrimination.

Avalanches cascade in the background of the western Norwegian port town, a visual metaphor for the impenetrable layers of icy, inhuman behavior that characterizes most Norwegians in the film (save Mia, who considers the situation with reason and beyond its legal precedent). The CPS representative who first tells Lisbet what’s going on is so clinical in her responses that it’s as if they were programmed ahead of time, not an ounce of empathy or discerning logic in her bones. Yet she acts on behalf of the state, in the name of principles with which almost anyone would agree. Among them: “You shouldn’t hit your kids.”

The original lawyer who represents them takes on the same unblinking, robotic tone before she bails on them as calmly as she signed up simply because they’re upset. There’s an irony to a rationalism that doesn’t consider the human soul. Take, for instance, a CPS representative insisting there’s no evidence that suggests children are better off with non-abusive biological parents than a set of foster parents if the kids and new parents get along—an idea that requires no research to debunk.

Up against the cold, overbearing, soulless characterization of a Norwegian CPS operating in the name of reducing risk, the Gheorghius’ strict, silly rules for their children come across as something they’ll merely have to mature past when they’re older and opposed to something that will ruin their lives. Mungiu accentuates the lack of rigidity by showing how easy it is for Elia and Emmanuel to break their parents’ rules when peer-pressured by Noora (Henrikke Lund Olsen), a reality anyone who grew up in a religious home knows is true.

As progressive as Norway’s ideals may be, and however much one might agree with them on paper, Mungiu draws out the maltreatment in forcing someone to conform to laws of a society that are against their relatively harmless beliefs. The one thing the Norwegian state does have is an absolutely gobstopping courtroom that hovers over the fjord with floor-to-ceiling windows brandishing the celestial glow of the mountainous region in the background of every shot.

Cinematographer Tudor Vladimir Panduru and colorist Andu Radu once again wed their efforts to create the most aesthetically pleasing film of Cannes thus far, as they did with R.M.N. in 2022—a chilly sky blue masks the region in a beauty that’s hard to appreciate amidst the operation of its society. Reinsve and Stan are terrific, playing the conservative matriarch and patriarch with a gentle, hushed desperation, quaking in the wake of losing their five children forever as if they already have.

As with R.M.N. , Mungiu is in top-shelf operation. Fjord is a triumphant film that tugs at the spiritual and soulful in all of us, regardless of nation, creed, faith, or the rejection of all three. What the court will rule in both cases, and whether or not the Gheorghius will get back their kids, pulses with a pregnant tension as the nearly two-and-a-half-hour film proceeds in what seems 30 minutes. And its end will have you falling off the edge of your seat.

Fjord premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival and will be released by NEON.

article_text:
H ome Alone meets Mad Max in this atmospheric seasonal chiller, named for Halloween and not a cheery greeting. A disease has wiped out most of humanity, leaving 16-year-old Pumpkin (Milly Shapiro) stranded alone in her rural family home in the middle of nowhere for the best part of four years. This classic American clapboard house has always been the perfect quaint yet unsettling place to celebrate Halloween, and she determines to uphold the family tradition and do just that, sending a radio broadcast to anyone listening to invite them to celebrate spooky season with her. Unfortunately, the message is picked up by some less than wholesome types, led by Thalia (Shannyn Sossamon), thus setting the stage for the proverbial to hit the fan.

It’s the first major screen role for Shapiro since her memorable debut as the little sister in Ari Aster’s Hereditary , and she is in almost every scene here, making for quite the showcase. It’s good casting: Pumpkin is an intriguing presence – at once young and old, presumably because she’s been fending for herself during such a key stage of her development. She’s not had any adult guidance since the age of 12 – arresting her development in some ways, while having to survive, be totally independent and grieve her entire family alone has simultaneously made her unusually tough in others.

This turns out to be invaluable in a horror film; it gives the script plenty of room to have her make naive decisions which are wholly justified, as well as to prove surprisingly resilient in ways that the character’s backstory supports. This gives a plausible, grounded core to the story’s more outlandish trappings, and the splendid production design – ranging from cosy cottagecore Halloween to a timeless Bates motel aesthetic – makes for an appealing storyworld. Hallowarrior is the feature debut of Ben Sottak, an experienced short film-maker, and on this evidence he’s likely to be worth keeping an eye out for.

"paragraph", "text": "对兰蒂·巴姆而言，陶土不仅是一种材料。它是记忆的容器、身体的延伸，也是与不可见之物建立联系的媒介。通过挑战传统容纳观念的形态，她的实践探讨了脆弱性、转化，以及承载与被承载的可能性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在与《ART AFRICA》的这次对话中，巴姆回顾了其雕塑背后的直觉创作过程、伊法（Ifá）的灵性共鸣，以及让艺术对诠释保持开放的重要性。作为“以微小音调”的一部分在军械库展出，她的作品是对物质性、自由以及静心倾听的无声力量的沉思。兰蒂·巴姆作品《Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa》在2026年第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展厅的装置现场。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉（Norr Cohan）。摄影：凯西·凯尔鲍夫 / CKA（Casey Kelbaugh / CKA）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ranti-Bam_Venice_Courtesy-the-artist-and-James-Cohan-New-York_Photo-by-Casey-Kelbaugh_6-1030x687.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆作品《Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa》在2026年第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展厅的装置现场。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉（Norr Cohan）。摄影：凯西·凯尔鲍夫 / CKA（Casey Kelbaugh / CKA）。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "苏泽特·贝尔-罗伯茨（Suzette Bell-Roberts）：你的艺术实践探讨了陶土、身体、记忆与灵性之间的关系。你对这些联系的理解是如何演变的，它们又是如何塑造你所创造的形态的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "兰蒂·巴姆：我渐趋认为这些事物是密不可分的。身体承载记忆，陶土承载记忆，两者都在不断被触觉、压力、时间和经验所塑造。我的作品不断回归关于自由与容纳的问题。承载某物意味着什么？我们如何承载我们自己、我们的历史、彼此？陶土使我能够以物理方式探讨这些问题，同时为那些我们能感知却未必能清晰表达的事物留出空间。兰蒂·巴姆作品《Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa》在2026年第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展厅的装置现场。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉（Norr Cohan）。摄影：凯西·凯尔鲍夫 / CKA（Casey Kelbaugh / CKA）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ranti-Bam_Venice_Courtesy-the-artist-and-James-Cohan-New-York_Photo-by-Casey-Kelbaugh_4-1030x687.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆作品《Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa》在2026年第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展厅的装置现场。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉（Norr Cohan）。摄影：凯西·凯尔鲍夫 / CKA（Casey Kelbaugh / CKA）。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你的雕塑挑战了关于容器外形或其功能的传统观念。是什么吸引你将容器作为一种艺术形式，你又是如何探讨它与人體的关系的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对我而言，容器是任何具有承载能力的物体。它不必是中空的或封闭的。一个平整的表面可以承载印记，一个词语可以承载意义，一个人可以承载记忆。我开始用圆雕形式进行创作，是因为它们能如此完整地传达内部与外部、开放与边界之间的关系——这也是我们在身体内部体验到的状态。比起功能，我更感兴趣的是容纳本身或许就具有解放性。容器的脆弱性也深深植根于人性。它能保护，但也可能破碎。我相信所有的瑕疵都是美丽的，不是尽管它们不完美，而是正是因为它们的不完美。兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 1》，2026年，手工成型黑色炻器，© Ranti Bam 2026。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍姆·尼尔森（Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-1_2026_JCG19301_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 1》，2026年，手工成型黑色炻器，© Ranti Bam 2026。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍姆·尼尔森（Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen）。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你的作品借鉴了约鲁巴（Yoruba）的灵性传统，尤其是与占卜和连接相关的伊法（Ifa）概念。你对这些传统的介入是如何塑造你的艺术语言和对陶土的理解的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我未必是以约鲁巴灵性作为出发点开始创作的。这些联系往往是在制作过程中自然显现的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第一个伊法诞生于一次尝试创作图腾的经历。我做好了陶土柱，却意识到自己不再想做图腾，尽管我也不太确定自己究竟想要什么。三天后，我回到工作室，全身心投入到创作中。这个系列就这样开始了。吸引我的是伊法与神明共融的灵性实践，以及与之同等重要的亲近之意。这两者都与我和陶土的关系、创作的亲密感，以及与超越我们自身的事物建立联系的可能性产生了深刻的共鸣。兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 2》，2026年，手工成型黑色炻器，© Ranti Bam 2026。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍姆·尼尔森（Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-2_2026_JCG19300_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 2》，2026年，手工成型黑色炻器，© Ranti Bam 2026。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍姆·尼尔森（Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen）。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在2026年威尼斯双年展上，你展出了五件题为《Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa》的雕塑，它们呈现出守护者的姿态。是什么启发了这些作品，你如何理解它们与空间及与之相遇的人们之间的关系？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我理解为什么这些雕塑会被视为守护者，但我更愿意让它们的身份保持开放。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对我而言，艺术的崇高之处在于它为我们的想象力和渴望漫游创造了隐喻空间。我认为这是艺术创作中最至关重要的部分，并十分小心不去干涉它。我们每个人都带着各自的历史和欲望来到我们所遭遇的事物面前，我发现美妙的是，一件作品能够容纳所有这些可能性，而无需执着于任何单一的意义。兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 3》，2026年，手工成型黑色炻器，© Ranti Bam 2026。鸣谢艺术家与纽约诺尔·科汉。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍姆·尼尔森（Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-3_2026_JCG19299_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 3》，2026年，手工黑陶，© 兰蒂·巴姆 2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍尔姆·尼尔森。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在您的创作过程中，您与黏土保持着紧密的身体联系，让这种材质回应您的动作和手势。这种互动如何塑造您雕塑的最终形态？偶发性在您的实践中又扮演了什么角色？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些年来，我和黏土发展出了一种深度的共生关系。我不依赖预先画好的草图。我从一个意图、一个想法开始，形态在创作过程中自然显现。随着我的作品规模不断扩大，我的手势也从拥抱和抓握转变为操纵和支撑……我还在努力用语言把这种感觉具象化。我着迷于我的意图与材料自身的可能性及局限性之间的这种协商。重量、重力、压力和平衡都发挥着各自的作用。偶发性是我的实践的根本。通常，超越我意图呈现出来的东西，要比我所能想象的任何事物都更有趣。兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 4》，2026年，手工黑陶，© 兰蒂·巴姆 2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍尔姆·尼尔森。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-4_2026_JCG19298_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 4》，2026年，手工黑陶，© 兰蒂·巴姆 2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍尔姆·尼尔森。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由科约·库奥（Koyo Kouoh）构思的2026年威尼斯双年展主题“微调”（In Minor Keys），邀请观众去关注更安静的表达、倾听与连接。您如何结合您的创作来诠释这一主题，特别是您对精神性、物质性以及不可见之物的探索？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我从“微调”（In Minor Keys）中感受到美妙之处，在于它邀请人们去注意那些原本可能被忽视的事物。为更安静的存在、认知和世界体验方式留出空间，本身就是一种慷慨。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我和黏土的关系就扎根于这种专注之中。创作需要倾听、耐心，以及顺其自然让事物在属于它们自己的时间里显现的意愿。我认为在这样一个过度关注可见性与确定性、并将可见性与价值混为一谈的世界里，科约的愿景有着某种尤为动人的力量。并非所有事物都需要自我宣告或解释。有时，仅仅为事物的体验创造条件就足够了。兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 5》，2026年，手工黑陶，© 兰蒂·巴姆 2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍尔姆·尼尔森。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-5_2026_JCG19297_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆，《Ifa 5》，2026年，手工黑陶，© 兰蒂·巴姆 2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：雅各布·弗里斯-霍尔姆·尼尔森。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您在军械库（Arsenale）展出的雕塑在黏土、建筑与创作历史之间展开了对话。军械库的环境是如何塑造您的展示的？您希望作品与周围环境之间碰撞出什么样的对话？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本身就由大地构成、经由人类双手改造的建筑中展出黏土作品，有一种奇妙的美感。军械库承载着它自身的劳作、生产与时间历史。它的体量和物质存在感让我思考，雕塑如何去栖居这个空间，而不仅仅是占据它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我并不一定要规定作品与周围环境之间的对话。我更倾向于让这些不同的历史共存，为人们建立自己的连接留下空间。兰蒂·巴姆“Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa”在第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展区安装现场，2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：凯西·凯尔巴赫 / CKA。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ranti-Bam_Venice_Courtesy-the-artist-and-James-Cohan-New-York_Photo-by-Casey-Kelbaugh_9-1030x687.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "兰蒂·巴姆“Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa”在第61届威尼斯双年展军械库展区安装现场，2026年。由艺术家及纽约诺尔·科汉画廊提供。摄影：凯西·凯尔巴赫 / CKA。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您的作品探讨了脆弱性、转化，以及物质世界与精神世界之间的关系。在您职业生涯的这个阶段，参加第61届威尼斯双年展对您意味着什么？您如何看待您的实践对“微调”（In Minor Keys）更广泛对话的贡献？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我从未过多考虑过去追求某种创作生涯。我远比这更感兴趣的是过一种富有创造力的生活，并全身心投入其中。我希望我的作品能为他人提供那种自由的一隅——去漫游、去想象，并在看似平凡的事物中找到属于他们自己的可能。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "At the Arsenale in Venice, Ranti Bam’s five sculptures, Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa , explore the relationship between body, memory and spirituality as part of the 61st Venice Biennale, In Minor Keys ."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For Ranti Bam, clay is more than a material. It is a vessel for memory, an extension of the body and a means of engaging with the unseen. Through forms that challenge conventional ideas of containment, her practice explores vulnerability, transformation and the possibilities of holding and being held."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In this conversation with ART AFRICA , Bam reflects on the intuitive processes behind her sculptures, the spiritual resonances of Ifá and the importance of allowing art to remain open to interpretation. Presented at the Arsenale as part of In Minor Keys , her work offers a meditation on materiality, freedom and the quiet power of paying attention. Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ranti-Bam_Venice_Courtesy-the-artist-and-James-Cohan-New-York_Photo-by-Casey-Kelbaugh_6-1030x687.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA.", "credit": "ART AFRICA"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Suzette Bell-Roberts: Your artistic practice explores the relationship between clay, the body, memory, and spirituality. How has your understanding of these connections evolved, and how do they shape the forms you create?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ranti Bam: I’ve come to see these things as increasingly inseparable. The body holds memory, clay holds memory, and both are constantly being shaped by touch, pressure, time and experience. My work keeps returning to questions of freedom and containment. What does it mean to hold something? How do we hold ourselves, our histories, one another? Clay allows me to explore these questions physically, while making room for things we can sense but cannot always articulate. Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ranti-Bam_Venice_Courtesy-the-artist-and-James-Cohan-New-York_Photo-by-Casey-Kelbaugh_4-1030x687.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA.", "credit": "ART AFRICA"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Your sculptures challenge traditional ideas of what a vessel should look like or how it should function. What draws you to the vessel as an artistic form, and how do you explore its relationship to the human body?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For me, a vessel is anything with the capacity to hold. It doesn’t need to be hollow or enclosed. A flat surface can hold an impression, a word can hold meaning, a person can hold memory. I began working with vessels in the round because they communicate so completely the relationship between interior and exterior, openness and boundary, conditions we also experience within our bodies. I’m less interested in function than in the possibility that containment itself can be liberating. The vessel’s fragility is also deeply human. It can protect, but it can break. I believe all flaws are beautiful, not despite their imperfections, but because of them. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 1 ‘, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAM_Ifa-1_2026_JCG19301_v1-687x1030.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 1 ‘, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.", "credit": "ART AFRICA"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Your work draws on Yoruba spiritual traditions, particularly the concept of Ifa , which relates to divination and connection. How has your engagement with these traditions shaped your artistic language and understanding of clay?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I don’t necessarily begin with Yoruba spirituality as a point of departure. These connections often reveal themselves through making."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The first Ifa emerged from an attempt to create totems. I’d made the clay columns but realised I no longer wanted to make totems, although I wasn’t quite sure what I wanted instead. Three nights later, I returned to the studio and fell into the work. That’s how the series began. What drew me to Ifá was its spiritual practice of communing with the divine, and equally, the meaning of drawing close. Both resonate deeply with my relationship with clay, the intimacy of making, and the possibility of connecting with something beyond ourselves. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 2′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.", "credit": "ART AFRICA"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "At the 2026 Venice Biennale, you present five sculptures titled Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa , which take on the presence of guardians. What informed these works, and how do you understand their relationship to the space and the people who encounter them?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I understand why the sculptures might be seen as guardians, but I prefer to leave their identities open."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For me, the majesty of art lies in the metaphorical space it creates for our imaginations and longings to wander. I consider this the most vital part of art-making and take great care not to interfere with it. We each bring our own histories and desires to what we encounter, and I find it beautiful that a work can hold all these possibilities without insisting on any one meaning. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 3′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. article_text:
At the Arsenale in Venice, Ranti Bam’s five sculptures, Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa , explore the relationship between body, memory and spirituality as part of the 61st Venice Biennale, In Minor Keys .

For Ranti Bam, clay is more than a material. It is a vessel for memory, an extension of the body and a means of engaging with the unseen. Through forms that challenge conventional ideas of containment, her practice explores vulnerability, transformation and the possibilities of holding and being held.

In this conversation with ART AFRICA , Bam reflects on the intuitive processes behind her sculptures, the spiritual resonances of Ifá and the importance of allowing art to remain open to interpretation. Presented at the Arsenale as part of In Minor Keys , her work offers a meditation on materiality, freedom and the quiet power of paying attention. Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA.

Suzette Bell-Roberts: Your artistic practice explores the relationship between clay, the body, memory, and spirituality. How has your understanding of these connections evolved, and how do they shape the forms you create?

Ranti Bam: I’ve come to see these things as increasingly inseparable. The body holds memory, clay holds memory, and both are constantly being shaped by touch, pressure, time and experience. My work keeps returning to questions of freedom and containment. What does it mean to hold something? How do we hold ourselves, our histories, one another? Clay allows me to explore these questions physically, while making room for things we can sense but cannot always articulate. Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA.

Your sculptures challenge traditional ideas of what a vessel should look like or how it should function. What draws you to the vessel as an artistic form, and how do you explore its relationship to the human body?

For me, a vessel is anything with the capacity to hold. It doesn’t need to be hollow or enclosed. A flat surface can hold an impression, a word can hold meaning, a person can hold memory. I began working with vessels in the round because they communicate so completely the relationship between interior and exterior, openness and boundary, conditions we also experience within our bodies. I’m less interested in function than in the possibility that containment itself can be liberating. The vessel’s fragility is also deeply human. It can protect, but it can break. I believe all flaws are beautiful, not despite their imperfections, but because of them. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 1 ‘, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.

Your work draws on Yoruba spiritual traditions, particularly the concept of Ifa , which relates to divination and connection. How has your engagement with these traditions shaped your artistic language and understanding of clay?

I don’t necessarily begin with Yoruba spirituality as a point of departure. These connections often reveal themselves through making.

The first Ifa emerged from an attempt to create totems. I’d made the clay columns but realised I no longer wanted to make totems, although I wasn’t quite sure what I wanted instead. Three nights later, I returned to the studio and fell into the work. That’s how the series began. What drew me to Ifá was its spiritual practice of communing with the divine, and equally, the meaning of drawing close. Both resonate deeply with my relationship with clay, the intimacy of making, and the possibility of connecting with something beyond ourselves. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 2′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.

At the 2026 Venice Biennale, you present five sculptures titled Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa , which take on the presence of guardians. What informed these works, and how do you understand their relationship to the space and the people who encounter them?

I understand why the sculptures might be seen as guardians, but I prefer to leave their identities open.

For me, the majesty of art lies in the metaphorical space it creates for our imaginations and longings to wander. I consider this the most vital part of art-making and take great care not to interfere with it. We each bring our own histories and desires to what we encounter, and I find it beautiful that a work can hold all these possibilities without insisting on any one meaning. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 3′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.

In your creative process, you maintain a close physical relationship with clay, allowing the material to respond to your movements and gestures. How does this interaction shape the final form of your sculptures, and what role does the unexpected play in your practice?

Over the years, clay and I have developed a deep symbiosis. I don’t work from preparatory drawings. I begin with an intention, an idea, and the forms emerge through making. As my work has grown in scale, my gestures have shifted from hugging and holding to manipulating and supporting…and I’m still trying to flesh out the words. I’m fascinated by this negotiation between my intentions and the material’s own possibilities and limitations. Weight, gravity, pressure and balance all have a part to play. The unexpected is fundamental to my practice. Often, what emerges beyond my intentions is far more interesting than anything I could have imagined. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 4′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.

The 2026 Venice Biennale, In Minor Keys , conceived by Koyo Kouoh, invites audiences to consider quieter forms of expression, listening, and connection. How do you interpret this theme in relation to your practice, especially your exploration of spirituality, materiality, and the unseen?

What I find beautiful about In Minor Keys is its invitation to pay attention to what might otherwise go unnoticed. There is a generosity in making space for quieter ways of being, knowing and experiencing the world.

My relationship with clay is rooted in this attentiveness. Making requires listening, patience and a willingness to allow things to emerge in their own time. I think there’s something particularly moving about Koyo’s vision in a world so preoccupied with visibility and certainty, and with conflating visibility with value. Not everything needs to announce or explain itself. Sometimes it’s enough to create the conditions for something to be experienced. Ranti Bam, ‘ Ifa 5′, 2026, Handbuilt black stoneware, © Ranti Bam 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photo by Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen.

Your sculptures at the Arsenale create a dialogue between clay, architecture, and histories of making. How did the Arsenale setting shape your presentation, and what conversations do you hope emerge between the works and their surroundings?

There’s something beautiful about exhibiting clay within a building itself made from earth, transformed by human hands. The Arsenale carries its own histories of labour, production and time. Its scale and material presence made me consider how the sculptures might inhabit the space rather than simply occupy it.

I don’t necessarily want to prescribe the conversation between the works and their surroundings. I prefer to let these different histories coexist, leaving room for people to make their own connections. Installation view of Ranti Bam,’ Ifa Ile Oja – Black Ifa ‘ at the Arsenale at the 61st Biennale di Venezia , 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Norr Cohan, New York. Photograph by Casey Kelbaugh / CKA.

Your work explores vulnerability, transformation, and the relationship between the physical and spiritual worlds. What does participating in the 61st Venice Biennale mean to you at this stage of your career, and how do you see your practice contributing to the wider conversations of In Minor Keys ?

I’ve never thought much about having a creative career. I’m far more interested in living a creative life and being present to it. I hope my work offers others something of that freedom, to wander, imagine and find their own possibilities in the seemingly ordinary.

title_original: Il Medioevo non è lontano: a Bologna una mostra mette in dialogo san Francesco e l’arte contemporanea
editorial_title_zh: 中世纪并不遥远：博洛尼亚一场展览将圣方济各与当代艺术展开对话

San Francesco tra Medioevo e Contemporaneo），展览现场", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个核心涉及万物之间的手足情谊，这一主题在圣方济各与狼的故事中找到了最具辨识度的表现形式之一。在法尔皮·维尼奥利（Farpi Vignoli）的雕塑周围，汇聚了一件来自方济各会圣殿的饰有鹿的十三世纪酒罐、路易·阿尔伯特·卡尔万（Louis Albert Carvin）的《瞪羚》与弗洛里亚诺·博迪尼（Floriano Bodini）的《鸽子》。由此浮现出一种超越人类维度并延伸至其他生命形式的手足情谊观念，使方济各会说教的核心内容之一重获现实意义，并在语言和驱动作品创作的原因存在距离的情况下，暗示了方济各会意象与现代对待动物世界的敏感性之间的连续性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "而身体与苦难的核心地位则由一件大十字架见证，该十字架归属于方济各会苦十字架大师（Maestro dei Crocifissi Francescani）作坊，可追溯至1270年左右，它见证了受苦基督（Christus patiens）模式的传播——在该模式中，沉浸于痛苦之中的基督身体取代了凯旋十字架的形象。正是在与这一形象的关系中，呈现了埃托雷·斯帕莱蒂为《新安布罗西圣歌集》（Nuovo Evangeliario Ambrosiano）创作的《扉页》以及卢乔·丰塔纳（Lucio Fontana）的一件《空间概念》。丰塔纳在其研究中标志着对作为界限的表面的超越之举，因此得以从一个不同的视角被观察，这一视角将物质的打开引向伤口的物理与象征维度：“尽管布里（Burri）对作品的灵性阐释一直保持谨慎，但这种并置从叙事角度来看是行之有效的，它再次证明了无形式艺术（arte informale）作品的多义性特征，即翁贝托·和可（Umberto Eco，1962）已经赋予它的‘开放作品’的属性，”批评文本中写道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "圣尼科洛德利阿尔巴里大师（Maestro di San Nicolò degli Albari）的双联画与西迪瓦尔·菲拉（Sidival Fila）的《红丝绒》（Velluto rosso）之间的对照，同样建立在甚至在主题之前的对物质的处理之上；物质保留了时间及其先前放置位置的痕迹，而其被撕裂的表面则让人联想起信仰的苦难和身体维度。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/04_Sorella_arte_San_Francesco_tra_Medioevo_e_Contemporaneo-1024x768.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "《艺术姐妹。中世纪与当代之间的圣方济各》（Sorella arte. San Francesco tra Medioevo e Contemporaneo），展览现场", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相反，在勒卡罗艺术博物馆，这种对比发生了逆转，并从二十世纪开始，从阿尔贝托·布里的《带点的黑色》（Nero con punti）开始，与里米尼的内里（Neri da Rimini）创作的一部抄本饰品以及毛里齐奥·奥斯蒂（Maurizio Osti）的《神曲》（Cantica）的三卷本并置。在此，人们强调了切萨雷·布兰迪（Cesare Brandi）先前已经阐述过的一种解读，即关于这位翁布里亚艺术家的《麻袋》（Sacchi）与方济各会修士服之间的亲缘关系，这也是由于共同的翁布里亚起源和黄麻的使用，但它被纳入了关于表面与物质、以及在它们的转化中识别一种对本质的不同观念的更广泛讨论之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/photo_2026-11-08_22-00-20-768x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不试图证明影响关系并仅凭策展力量勾勒出一条路径的选择，构成了一个展览的巨大优势，这个展览在规模上非常小，但却能够避免将对话变成一种虚假的人文谱系重构。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/photo_2026-11-08_22-00-15-768x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《艺术姊妹》的价值因此大概就安放在其所采用的视角中，安放在它捕捉那些从根本上一直滋养并赋予艺术活力的联系、并以一种并不流于俗套的方式将其凸显出来的能力之中，从而突显并有时激发跨越时空的艺术品之间的关系。中世纪并未被赋予现代性，当代艺术也未被归约为某种宗教传统，而是选择利用这两个时期之间的距离来滋养一种积极且绝不平庸的对话前提。这是一个并非全无歧义的空间，展览试图通过图像的持久性及其持续产生解读的能力去对之发问，即便在它们诞生的历史条件之外亦是如此。从这个意义上说，配合展览出版的珍贵研究成果至关重要，这是一本收录了作品说明以及法梅利和马萨切西的批评长文的双语目录。", "translated": true}]

Il Medioevo non viene attualizzato e il contemporaneo non è ricondotto a una tradizione religiosa, e si sceglie piuttosto di servirsi della distanza tra i due momenti per alimentare il presupposto di un confronto attivo e mai banale. article_text:
A ottocento anni dalla morte di san Francesco d’Assisi, il suo immaginario torna a essere interrogato con un confronto che attraversa otto secoli di storia dell’arte. A Bologna , Sorella arte. San Francesco tra Medioevo e Contemporaneo , a cura di Mark Gregory D’Apuzzo , Giovanni Gardini , Pasquale Fameli e Fabio Massaccesi , si sviluppa in due sedi – il Museo Civico Medievale e il Museo d’arte Lercaro – fino al 17 gennaio 2027, mettendo in relazione testimonianze figurative della cultura francescana e opere di artisti del Novecento e della contemporaneità. Il progetto, promosso dai Musei Civici d’Arte Antica del Comune di Bologna e dalla Fondazione Museo d’arte Cardinale Giacomo Lercaro ETS, include Lucio Fontana , Alberto Burri , Ettore Spalletti , Giuseppe Penone , Floriano Bodini , Sidival Fila , Maurizio Osti , Aldo Borgonzoni e altri protagonisti dell’arte contemporanea in un dialogo con opere di artisti del XIII e XIV secolo, e prende le mosse da una domanda che riguarda la persistenza di un immaginario religioso e il modo in cui le immagini continuano a produrre significati anche quando vengono sottratte al proprio contesto originario.

«Gli accostamenti proposti non intendono dimostrare continuità storiche, filiazioni o influenze, né ricondurre le opere contemporanee entro un improbabile alveo francescano. Costruiscono piuttosto un sistema di risonanze, nel quale opere lontanissime per cronologia, linguaggio e contesto sono poste in tensione reciproca, lasciando emergere assonanze inattese e nuovi orizzonti di significato, spesso destinati a manifestarsi proprio nello spazio aperto dal loro incontro», spiegano i curatori Pasquale Fameli e Fabio Massaccesi.

Il punto di partenza è l’ottavo centenario della morte del santo, che la mostra sceglie di tradurre assumendo la figura di Francesco come un orizzonte interpretativo attraverso cui mettere alla prova la possibilità di un incontro tra opere storicamente lontane. Il titolo, Sorella arte , richiama inevitabilmente il lessico del Cantico delle creature , ma suggerisce anche una relazione che non si esaurisce nella comune appartenenza a una tradizione; le opere vengono infatti accostate senza che sia necessario individuare una filiazione o una diretta continuità stilistica. Una simile impostazione si inserisce nella riflessione che negli ultimi decenni ha interessato la storia dell’arte e le pratiche curatoriali e che ha messo in discussione la necessità di organizzare le opere esclusivamente secondo successioni cronologiche, scuole e movimenti. Da Aby Warburg a Georges Didi-Huberman , passando per gli studi di Walter Benjamin , il montaggio delle immagini è stato considerato uno strumento capace di produrre conoscenza e far emergere relazioni che non coincidono necessariamente con i rapporti storici di influenza. E «se la comprensione si compie nella Horizontverschmelzung (“fusione degli orizzonti”), l’accostamento proposto dalla mostra assume invece la permanenza della distanza come condizione fondante della conoscenza. Il significato non si esaurisce nelle singole opere: trova nell’accostamento una nuova possibilità di emergere». La mostra si serve in tal modo proprio delle distanze che intercorrono fra le immagini per produrre un senso autonomo.

La scelta di organizzare tale esposizione a Bologna guarda al rapporto tra la città e il francescanesimo, che risale agli anni immediatamente successivi alla fondazione dell’Ordine. La presenza dei Frati Minori è documentata già tra il 1211 e il 1212, quando Bernardo di Quintavalle diede avvio al primo insediamento presso Santa Maria delle Pugliole. Pochi anni dopo, secondo la testimonianza di Tommaso Arcidiacono di Spalato , Francesco avrebbe predicato in città il 15 agosto 1222, durante la festa dell’Assunzione. Il suo passaggio, ricordato per il celebre incipit del sermone – «gli angeli, gli uomini, i demoni» – rappresenta una delle testimonianze più significative dell’incontro tra il mondo universitario medievale e il movimento minoritico. La successiva costruzione della basilica di San Francesco, avviata nel 1236 e sostanzialmente completata entro il 1263, avrebbe consolidato ulteriormente il ruolo di Bologna nella diffusione dell’Ordine.

Il racconto si dipana dunque in due ambienti, costringe ad attraversare fisicamente la città – che in qualche modo entra a far parte a tutti gli effetti della mostra – e si sviluppa in maniera sottilmente diversa fra le due sedi. Le due istituzioni propongono infatti due differenti modalità di avvicinarsi alle opere, una più direttamente legata alla ricostruzione storica e alla conservazione del patrimonio medievale, l’altra caratterizzata da una vocazione al confronto tra arte antica e contemporanea. Inoltre, il Museo Civico Medievale si concentra innanzitutto sulla presenza francescana nella città e sulle sue ricadute nella produzione figurativa, ricostruendo soprattutto la presenza storica e figurativa del francescanesimo, mentre Museo d’arte Lercaro ne amplia le possibilità interpretative e assume quelle stesse testimonianze come interlocutrici di una ricerca contemporanea che non ha necessariamente Francesco come riferimento diretto. Due narrazioni sono complementari e al contempo distinte, legate dalla stessa leggerezza di allestimento – pur in un ambiente inevitabilmente molto “denso” – e dal dialogo che dà voce alla relazione fra le opere.

Al Museo Civico Medievale, questa dimensione emerge soprattutto attraverso opere che restituiscono il radicamento del culto nella vita cittadina. Il San Francesco realizzato intorno al 1390 da Jacobello e Pierpaolo Dalle Masegne proveniente dalla Loggia della Mercanzia, ad esempio, faceva parte di un gruppo comprendente la Giustizia e i santi protettori di Bologna. In questo caso, la presenza del santo accanto alle figure che incarnavano la protezione della comunità mostra come la sua immagine avesse ormai superato l’ambito strettamente devozionale e fosse a tutti gli effetti entrata nella rappresentazione pubblica della città. I disegni di Edoardo Collamarini per la basilica di San Francesco ampliano questo riferimento, riportando l’attenzione sull’edificio che ha contribuito a definire la presenza minoritica nel tessuto urbano.

Un altro nucleo riguarda la fraternità tra le creature, tema che trova una delle sue espressioni più riconoscibili nell’episodio di Francesco e il lupo. Intorno alla scultura di Farpi Vignoli sono riuniti un boccale duecentesco con cervo proveniente dalla basilica francescana, le Gazzelle di Louis Albert Carvin e la Colomba di Floriano Bodini. Ne emerge un’idea di fraternità che oltrepassa la dimensione umana e si estende alle altre forme del vivente, restituendo attualità a uno dei nuclei centrali della predicazione francescana , s uggerendo una continuità tra l’immaginario francescano e una sensibilità moderna nei confronti del mondo animale, pur nella distanza dei linguaggi e delle ragioni che hanno guidato la realizzazione delle opere.

La centralità del corpo e della sofferenza è testimoniata invece dalla grande Croce attribuita alla bottega del Maestro dei Crocifissi Francescani , databile intorno al 1270, che testimonia la diffusione del modello del Christus patiens , nel quale il corpo di Cristo, reclinato nel dolore, sostituisce l’immagine del Crocifisso trionfante. È in rapporto a questa immagine che vengono presentati il Frontespizio di Ettore Spalletti, realizzato per il Nuovo Evangeliario Ambrosiano, e un Concetto spaziale di Lucio Fontana. Il gesto di Fontana, che nella sua ricerca segna il superamento della superficie come limite, viene così osservato da una prospettiva diversa, che fa dell’apertura della materia un richiamo alla dimensione fisica e simbolica della ferita: «Per quanto Burri fosse restio alle interpretazioni spirituali della sua opera, l’accostamento risulta funzionale dal punto di vista narrativo, dimostrando una volta di più il carattere polisemico dell’opera d’arte informale, la condizione di ‘opera aperta’ che Umberto Eco (1962) gli aveva già assegnato», si legge nel testo critico.

Anche il confronto tra il dittico del Maestro di San Nicolò degli Albari e Velluto rosso di Sidival Fila si fonda su una relazione che riguarda la materia prima ancora che il soggetto; la materia conserva le tracce del tempo e della propria precedente collocazione, mentre la sua superficie lacerata richiama la sofferenza e la dimensione corporea della fede.

Al Museo d’arte Lercaro, invece, il confronto si ribalta e parte dal Novecento, a cominciare da Nero con punti di Alberto Burri, accostato a un codice miniato da Neri da Rimini e ai tre volumi della Cantica di Maurizio Osti . Si sottolinea in questo caso una lettura già formulata da Cesare Brandi circa la prossimità tra i Sacchi dell’artista umbro e il saio di Francesco, anche in ragione della comune origine umbra e dell’impiego della juta, ma la si inserisce in un più ampio discorso sulla superficie e sulla materia, e sulla possibilità di riconoscere nella loro trasformazione una diversa concezione dell’essenziale.

La scelta di non dimostrare rapporti di influenza e di tracciare un percorso con la sola forza curatoriale rappresenta un grande punto di forza in una mostra che è molto piccola a livello di dimensioni, ma che riesce a non trasformare il dialogo in una ricostruzione genealogica artificiosa.

Il valore di Sorella arte risiede quindi, probabilmente, nello sguardo adottato, nella capacità di cogliere legami – che, in fondo, nutrono e danno linfa all’arte da sempre – e di metterli in evidenza in maniera non scontata, evidenziando e talvolta facendo scaturire relazioni fra opere lontane nel tempo. Il Medioevo non viene attualizzato e il contemporaneo non è ricondotto a una tradizione religiosa, e si sceglie piuttosto di servirsi della distanza tra i due momenti per alimentare il presupposto di un confronto attivo e mai banale. Uno spazio, non sempre privo di ambiguità, che la mostra prova a interrogare con la persistenza delle immagini e la loro capacità di continuare a generare letture, anche al di fuori delle condizioni storiche in cui sono nate. Fondamentale, in questo senso, il prezioso lavoro di studio pubblicato in occasione della mostra, un catalogo bilingue che raccoglie le schede delle opere e il saggio critico di Fameli e Massaccesi.

article_text:
昨年10月に東京・西麻布から表参道へと移転したギャラリー「ア・ライトハウス・カナタ」。移転1周年を記念した展覧会「Ars Longa, Vita Brevis（アルス・ロンガ ヴィータ・ブレヴィス）」が10月30日まで開催されています。

ア・ライトハウス・カナタは、2007年の設立以来、 21世紀における現代日本美術の再評価に取り組み、多様な視点から現代美術の境界を拡張することを目指しています。

本展では、田中信行や尾崎悟をはじめ、これまで国内外で紹介してきた作家たちによる新作・代表作を中心に、およそ50点の作品が展示されています。ジャンルや世代、素材、技法の異なる作品が一堂に会することで、ア・ライトハウス・カナタがこれまで大切にしてきた美意識を、ひとつの空間の中で多角的に体感できる機会となります。

展覧会名「Ars Longa, Vita Brevis」は、「芸術は長く、人生は短い」を意味するラテン語に由来します。限られた時間の中で生き、制作する作家たちの精神と、その時間を超えて残り続ける作品。そこにある時間の隔たりに目を向けることで、芸術が持つ普遍性と、その一瞬にしか生まれ得ない表現の価値を見つめます。移転1周年をひとつの節目として、作家たちが生み出す作品とその美意識を通して、これまでの歩みを振り返るとともに、その先にある新たな可能性を提示します。

また会期中は、1階のメインギャラリーに加え、通常はプライベートな空間として使用している2階ギャラリーも特別に開放されます。1階とは異なる空間で、作品との新たな出会いを楽しむことができます。

参加アーティスト（一部）

田中信行（たなか・のぶゆき）

1959年東京都生まれ。1983年東京藝術大学美術学部工芸科卒業、1985年同大学大学院美術研究科漆芸専攻修了。日本の伝統的な漆芸技法を基盤としながら、漆を現代彫刻の素材として捉え直し、独自の立体表現を追求する。幾重にも塗り重ねられた漆の深い光沢と、滑らかで有機的な曲面を特徴とし、内側と外側、空間と形態の関係性を探求している。伝統工芸の枠組みを超え、漆という素材の造形的・精神的な可能性を現代美術の領域へと広げてきた。国内外の美術館や展覧会で作品を発表し、漆による現代彫刻の新たな表現を切り拓いている。

尾崎悟（おざき・さとる）

1963年東京都生まれ。1993年東京藝術大学大学院修了。現在は千葉県を拠点に制作活動を続ける。ステンレス鋼を主な素材とし、金属を叩き、磨き上げる高度な技術によって、硬質な素材から柔らかさや生命感を感じさせる独自の彫刻表現を追求する。鏡面に磨き上げられた表面と、流麗で有機的なフォルムを特徴とし、周囲の光や空間を映し込みながら、見る角度によって異なる表情を生み出す。金属という素材の可能性を独自の造形によって広げ、国内外で作品を発表している。作品はヒューストン美術館、龍美術館、富邦美術館などに収蔵されている。

三鑰彩音（Ayane Mikagi）

1988年神奈川県生まれ。2017年多摩美術大学大学院美術研究科絵画専攻日本画研究領域修了。2021年まで同大学日本画研究室助手を務める。花や自然の風景を主な題材に、日本画の伝統的な素材や技法を生かしながら、鮮やかな色彩と大胆な構図による独自の絵画世界を展開する。具象と抽象の境界を行き来する表現を特徴とし、自然の持つ生命感や移ろいゆく美しさを、華やかさと繊細さを兼ね備えた画面に描き出している。

2026年11月4日（水）から21日（土）まで、ア・ライトハウス・カナタにて個展「Scents Infused」を開催予定。

◆出品作家 斉藤義重、菅井汲、堂本尚郎、尾崎悟、深見陶治、安田侃、生田丹代子、三原研、岸映子、木村芳郎、杉谷恵造、森山寛二郎、米元優曜、冨樫葉子、津守秀憲、藤掛幸智、横山翔平、レイモンド愛華、武山直樹、佐故龍平、加藤貢介、横山修、Joseph Walsh、亘章吾、田中信行、中田真裕、柞磨祥子、小梛真弓、三尾瑠璃、深水沙由理、福田笑子、朝倉隆文、三鑰彩音、武井地子、佐藤健太郎、村松辰之介、大島幸子、前田正憲、松田啓佑、長谷川幾与、谷川将樹、中野優 （順不同・敬称略）

ア・ライトハウス・カナタ / A Lighthouse called Kanata

2007年の設立以来、ア・ライトハウス・カナタは21世紀における現代日本美術の再評価に取り組み、多様な視点から現代美術の境界を拡張することを目指しています。美的伝統の再発見と進化を通じて、カナタは日本国内外のアーティストによる抽象絵画や彫刻に焦点を当て、素材へのこだわりを通じて新たな美の概念を創造しています。

年間5～6回の展覧会を開催し、12～14の国際アートフェアに出展。また、新進気鋭のアーティストから、確立されたベテラン作家までを記録・紹介する出版活動を通じて、そのプログラムをさらに充実させています。さらに、メトロポリタン美術館（ニューヨーク）、ヴィクトリア＆アルバート美術館（ロンドン）、龍美術館（上海）など、世界の主要な文化機関と協力し、ギャラリーの独自の視点と美学を国際的な舞台で発信するためのプラットフォームを創出。2025年秋、東京・表参道の自社ビルへの移転。さらなる日本美術の未來への架け橋となることを目指しています。

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）

今年秋天,东京·表参道的转移到自己的建筑,旨在成为日本艺术未来的架子桥。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "(阅读《艺术展》纳比编辑团)", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A.Lighthouse 卡纳塔 表入路 1 周年纪念小组展“Ars article_text:
Aimee Harrison and Lucía Sanromán will curate the 2027 edition of the Liverpool Biennial, titled The Age of Magical Thinking . The exhibition is scheduled to take place from 5 June to 19 September.

The theme draws on psychologist Jean Piaget’s theory of cognitive development, which identified a period in childhood development where imagination is particularly strong. The exhibition will position childhood, a transitional period charged with creative potential, as a lens through which to consider our current global crisis.

‘I think of childhood and youth as a period of constant transition, of change and possibility, but also a time that demands and requires the urgency to question the present’, said Sanromán in a statement. ‘Artists in the exhibition give us insights into the imagination of childhood, spurring us to boldly ask for a better future. The exhibition responds to the loud demands by young people throughout the world to be taken seriously in how political decisions are made, and for whom.’

The participating artists are:

Ad Minoliti ; Amalia Pica, Anya Paintsil; Charmaine Poh; Dor Guez ; EBB.Global; Elias Nafaa; Francis Alÿs ; Harold Offeh; Hiroko Kubo; Immy Mali; Iván Argote ; the vacuum cleaner; Laakkuluk Williamson; Wen Cheng Lee; Marilyn Boror Bor; Petrit Halilaj ; Rineke Dijkstra; Robert Gabris; Ronak & Roza Moshtaghi; Ruth Ewan; Tania Candani ; Yarema Malashchuk & Roman Khimei ; Zohra Opoku.
